Your Application for admission
You are here: Home / Prospective Students / Your Application for admission
The Berkeley – UCSF Graduate Program in Bioengineering welcomes applications for the PhD in bioengineering from outstanding, highly motivated students with a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in related fields. See our eligibility details for more information.
DEADLINE: December 1, 8:59 PM PST
Applications are accepted for fall entry only and admitted applicants are expected to join the program on schedule, the fall semester of their admission year – e.g. fall 2027 for students who apply in fall 2026. Please plan your application accordingly.
The application must be submitted through Berkeley’s online graduate application system no later than December 1. Supporting materials, such as transcripts, recommendation letters, and GRE and TOEFL scores, should arrive no later than December 1.
All applications and supporting materials are submitted electronically through the application portal. Listed below are required components of the application you must submit in order to be considered for admission into the Bioengineering graduate programs. See detailed instructions at the Graduate Division.
We recommend that applicants complete their applications as early as possible and be sure to hit the submit button before the deadline.
Apply now
Academic Records
You are required to upload unofficial transcripts for all schools that you have attended. Applicants who studied outside the United States in non-English speaking institutions must upload the English translated transcripts. Uploaded files must be in PDF format and no larger than 8 MB. Please make sure that your social security number (SSN) does not appear on your transcript (if it does, black it out before uploading the document).
(Please note that even if you have not yet finished your coursework when you apply, we still require a current transcript from you. If you are admitted, at that time, we will ask you submit a final official transcript showing the degree awarded to complete our records.)
For more information about transcripts, please see the Graduate Division Admissions Information.
Those those who have attended an international university must convert their grades to the U.S. system. Please visit the gpa conversion page.
Application Essays
These essays are very important to the application process and should be taken seriously. These are two separate essays.
The Statement of Purpose asks:
Please describe your aptitude and motivation for graduate study in your area of specialization, including your preparation for this field of study, your academic plans or research interests in your chosen area of study, Professors whose research interests parallel yours, and your future career goals. Please be specific about why UC Berkeley/UCSF would be a good intellectual match for you. Brevity is appreciated – no more than two pages. Please see the graduate writing guide for more information.
The Personal History Statement asks:
In an essay, describe how your background and life experiences have influenced your decision to pursue a graduate degree at this time. Please see the graduate writing guide for more information.
Letters of Recommendation
Three letters of recommendation, at least two of which should be written by faculty. All reviewers should be familiar with the applicant’s scholarly abilities.
Having more than 3 letters, although allowed, is not recommended. Due to the volume of applications we receive every year, there is no guarantee that more than 3 letters will be read. Three strong letters is much better than 3 strong letters and one mediocre or bad letter.
It can be a good idea to ask your recommenders if they can write you a good, detailed letter. The best letters gauge your ability and potential for research and graduate study, often citing examples from the recommenders own experiences with you.
Letters of recommendation will be gathered electronically as part of the online application. Also complete the Recommendation Waiver Form in the application package.
Specialty Area of Study
On the application you must selected a first and second specialty area of study. The main purpose of this section is to guide us in determining which faculty members are best suited to review your application. The areas to choose from are:
Biomaterials, Cell and Tissue Engineering
Biomedical Imaging
BioMems & Nanotechnology
Computational Biology and Genomics
Neural Systems Engineering & Vision Science
Systems & Synthetic Biology
Evidence of English Language Proficiency
For Fall 2027, tests taken before June 1, 2025 will not be accepted.
All applicants who have completed a basic degree in a country/region in which the official language is not English are required to submit official evidence of English language proficiency, the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS).
The department of bioengineering requires the same scores set by the Graduate Division: 90 on the TOEFL taken before January 20, 2026, 5 on the TOEFL taken on or after January 21, 2026, or 7 on the IELTS. The institution code for UC Berkeley is 4833 for Graduate Programs.
See complete details at the Graduate Division.
GRE
The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) became optional for all applicants beginning the Fall 2020 admission cycle. See more information on our FAQ.
ETS will not report test scores older than 5 years.
If choosing to submit, the exam is composed of three sections: Analytical Writing, Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning. We do NOT require a subject test.
For more information about the test, as well as locations, test dates, and the time it will take for score reports to reach Berkeley, please consult the Educational Testing Service (ETS). They can be reached at (609) 771-7670. Inquiries can also be made to gre-info@ets.org and http://www.gre.org.
The institution code for Berkeley is 4833 and the Department code is 1603.
Application Fee
You must submit an application fee when you apply. The application fee is not refundable. Payments are accepted by credit card only. See details online.
U.S. citizens or permanent residents who can demonstrate financial need are eligible to apply for a waiver of the application fee. See guidelines for waivers. Please note: The bioengineering program does not offer a separate fee waiver program.
Resume or CV
Please upload a recent version of your resume or curriculum vitae.
Application Completion
Upon submission you will receive an email confirming your submission. You may log back in to your application status page to monitor materials received or processed, such as: fee waivers, test scores, letters of recommendation, and admission decision. When test scores are matched they will show as “verified”.
Potential applicants facing undue hardships in submitting application materials due to major natural disasters should contact bioe-grad@berkeley.edu
